What is printed by this program?

40 END

30 PRINT Y
40 END

questions.explanation: Brushes give strokes such as calligraphy, oil and watercolour effects.

questions.stem: In Paint, to draw a perfect circle with the ellipse (oval) tool, the user holds down the
questions.explanation: Holding Shift keeps the width and height equal, giving a circle.

questions.stem: In Paint, the select tool is used to
options: mark part of a picture so it can be moved, copied or deleted
erase the whole canvas at once and start a new picture
fill an area of the picture with a colour of your choice
draw straight lines between any two chosen points on the picture
questions.explanation: Selecting an area lets the user work on just that part.

questions.stem: In Paint, the magnifier (zoom) tool is used to
options: print the picture at a larger size on a bigger sheet of paper
enlarge the view of part of the picture for detailed work
make the file smaller so that it takes up less disk space
save the picture in a new folder under a different name
questions.explanation: Zooming in makes small details easier to see and edit.

questions.stem: In Paint, holding down the Shift key while using the line tool helps to
options: draw lines at exact fixed angles
questions.explanation: Shift restricts the line to fixed angles.

questions.stem: To turn a picture in Paint upside down, the user should use the
questions.explanation: The rotate/flip commands turn the picture or selection over.

questions.stem: Which list contains only spreadsheet packages?
questions.explanation: These three programs arrange data in rows and columns and perform calculations.

questions.stem: Which of the following tasks is best done with a spreadsheet package?
options: Drawing a cartoon for the school magazine
Browsing the internet for news and sports
Typing a long story for a class competition
questions.explanation: Spreadsheets calculate totals and differences in budgets automatically.

questions.stem: In a spreadsheet, columns are labelled with
questions.explanation: Columns are named A, B, C and so on, while rows are numbered.

questions.stem: In a spreadsheet, rows run
options: across the worksheet (horizontally) and are numbered
only in charts, where they are used to label the bars
down the worksheet and are lettered from A to Z and on
diagonally from the top left to the bottom right corner
questions.explanation: Rows are horizontal and are labelled 1, 2, 3 and so on.

questions.stem: In the formula =SUM(A1:A10), the part A1:A10 is called a
questions.explanation: A range is a group of adjacent cells named by its first and last cells.

questions.stem: The cell that is currently selected and ready to receive data is called the
questions.explanation: The active cell is outlined with a thick border and its address appears in the name box.

questions.stem: The range made up of the cells in row 2 from column C to column F is written as
questions.explanation: A range is written as the first cell address, a colon and the last cell address, with the column letter before the row number.

questions.stem: One way of loading Microsoft Excel is to
options: double-click the Excel icon on the desktop
press the power button twice and then wait
switch off the monitor and then restart it
open the Paint program and choose Spreadsheet
questions.explanation: Double-clicking the program icon (or choosing it from the Start menu) starts Excel.

questions.stem: To edit the content of a cell, the user can
options: double-click the cell or press F2
questions.explanation: Double-clicking or pressing F2 puts the cell in edit mode.

questions.stem: To make a column wider so that its contents fit, the user can
options: type the text again in a smaller font in the same column
delete the column and insert a new one beside the next column
drag the boundary line to the right of the column heading
press Ctrl + P and choose a bigger page size from the menu
questions.explanation: Dragging the column boundary changes the column width.

questions.stem: The spreadsheet function used to add up a range of numbers is
questions.explanation: SUM adds all the numbers in a range.

questions.stem: Cells A1 to A4 contain 10, 20, 30 and 40. What does =SUM(A1:A4) return?
Cell B2 contains 5 (quantity) and C2 contains 1200 (price in naira). What does =B2*C2 return?
questions.explanation: 5 x 1200 = 6000, the total cost in naira.

questions.stem: The spreadsheet function that counts how many cells in a range contain numbers is
questions.explanation: COUNT returns the number of cells with numeric entries.

questions.stem: The function =MAX(B1:B10) returns the
questions.explanation: MAX gives the highest number; MIN gives the lowest.

questions.stem: Cell A1 contains 150 and B1 contains 6. What does =A1/B1 return?
Cell A1 contains 3 and B1 contains 4. What does =(A1+B1)*2 return?
questions.explanation: The brackets are worked first: 3 + 4 = 7, then 7 x 2 = 14.

questions.stem: Cell C1 contains the formula =A1+B1. If this formula is copied down to C2, the formula in C2 becomes
questions.explanation: Relative cell references adjust to the new row when a formula is copied.

questions.stem: A wide worksheet with many columns is best printed with the page set to
options: portrait orientation with tiny margins only
questions.explanation: Landscape pages are wider than they are tall, so more columns fit across.

questions.stem: A database is
options: a single picture stored on a computer
a type of printer used in large offices
a computer virus that deletes stored records
an organised collection of related data
questions.explanation: Databases store related data in an organised way for easy retrieval.

questions.stem: A field that uniquely identifies each record in a table, such as a student's admission number, is called the
questions.explanation: No two records have the same key value.

questions.stem: A collection of related records, such as the records of all students in a school, is called a
questions.explanation: Related records grouped together form a file or table.

questions.stem: A student's name is not a good choice for the key field of a school database because
options: names cannot be typed into a number field
names are too short to be stored in a table
two students may have the same name
names change every day in the school register
questions.explanation: A key must be unique, so a number such as the admission number is used.

questions.stem: A database that stores all its data in one single table is a
questions.explanation: A flat file has one table with no links to others.

questions.stem: A database in which records are arranged in a tree-like structure of parents and children is a
questions.explanation: In a hierarchical database each child record has one parent, like branches of a tree.

questions.stem: Which type of chart is best for comparing the number of students in five different classes?
options: Pie chart of one class only
Line graph of the time of day
questions.explanation: Column charts compare separate quantities side by side.

questions.stem: Before inserting a chart in a spreadsheet, the user should first
options: print the worksheet and check the figures
close the workbook and open a blank one
select the data range to be plotted
delete the data and leave only the headings
questions.explanation: The chart is drawn from the selected cells.

questions.stem: A column chart can be changed to a pie chart by using the
options: Save As command on the menu
questions.explanation: Change Chart Type converts an existing chart into another type.

questions.stem: A chart in Excel is linked to its worksheet data, so when a value in the data is changed, the chart
questions.explanation: Charts are drawn from the cells, so they change when the cells change.

questions.stem: Labels such as 'Subjects' and 'Scores' placed beside the horizontal and vertical axes of a chart are called
questions.explanation: Axis titles explain what each axis shows.

questions.stem: Numbers shown on top of each bar or on each pie slice to give its exact value are called
questions.explanation: Data labels display the values represented by each bar or slice.

questions.stem: Third generation computers were the first to be widely used with
options: keyboards, monitors and operating systems instead of punched cards alone
artificial intelligence that could speak and understand human languages
vacuum tubes only, which filled large rooms and gave off a great deal of heat
touch screens and voice commands on small handheld phones and tablets
questions.explanation: With integrated circuits, users began to interact through keyboards and screens controlled by operating systems.

questions.stem: First generation computers were programmed mainly in
questions.explanation: Early computers understood only machine code, which made programming slow and difficult.

questions.topic: Definition of data and data processing
questions.stem: Data processing means
options: converting raw data into meaningful information
cleaning the keyboard and other parts of a computer
buying a new computer and loading it with programs
switching off a computer after storing all the work
questions.explanation: Processing organises and calculates data so that it becomes useful information.

questions.topic: Definition of data and data processing
questions.stem: A teacher has the test scores of 40 students. Which of these is information produced from the data?
options: The class average calculated from all the scores
The list of scores before any calculation
questions.explanation: The average results from processing the scores, so it is information.

questions.stem: Registering for an examination by filling a form on a website is an example of
questions.explanation: Many examinations in Nigeria now require candidates to register online.

questions.stem: Checking examination results on an examination body's website shows the internet being used for
options: printing money through an online bank account
repairing computers at the examination centre
entertainment through games and video clips
questions.explanation: Results posted online can be checked from any place with internet access.

questions.stem: Compared with posting a letter, sending an e-mail is
questions.explanation: E-mail is delivered within seconds anywhere in the world at little cost.

questions.stem: For safe and comfortable typing, the keyboard should be placed so that the
options: forearms are roughly level and the elbows are bent at about a right angle
keyboard is on the floor and the user bends forward to reach the keys
wrists are bent sharply upwards and rest hard on the edge of the desk all the time
keyboard is at shoulder height so that the arms are raised while typing
questions.explanation: A correct keyboard height reduces strain on the shoulders, arms and wrists.

questions.stem: A computer virus is so called because, like a biological virus, it
options: is caused by dust and damp inside the system unit
copies itself and spreads from one computer to another
is a living organism that feeds on stored files and programs
can be seen with a microscope on the surface of the disk
questions.explanation: Computer viruses replicate and spread, just as biological viruses infect cells.

questions.stem: Downloading free games from unknown websites can
options: make the computer immune to viruses
questions.explanation: Untrusted downloads often carry hidden malicious software.

questions.stem: In a histogram, the bars
options: are always circles divided into sectors for each of the classes of data
show parts of a whole, with the whole being represented by one long bar
are drawn as dots joined by straight lines to show changes in the data
touch each other because the data is grouped into continuous classes
questions.explanation: Histograms display continuous grouped data, so there are no gaps between bars.

questions.stem: To print only part of a worksheet, such as the cells A1 to F20, the user should first
options: insert a chart over those cells
set that range as the print area
change the font of those cells
delete all the other cells in the sheet
questions.explanation: Setting a print area tells the program to print only the selected cells.

questions.stem: The shortcut Ctrl + A in a word processor is used to
options: select all the text in the document
add a new blank page to the document
print the document on the default printer
align all the text to the left margin
questions.explanation: Ctrl + A highlights the whole document so it can be formatted at once.

questions.stem: The person in charge of planning and directing the computer department of an organisation is the
questions.explanation: The computer manager oversees the staff, equipment and services of the computer unit.

questions.stem: In a database program such as Microsoft Access, a query is used to
options: find records that meet certain conditions
questions.explanation: For example, a query can list all students who scored above 70.

questions.stem: A smartphone can do most things a GSM phone does and also
options: browse the internet and run applications
questions.explanation: Smartphones are small computers with internet access and apps.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the main electronic component used in each of the first four generations of computers. [4 marks]
(b) State two features of fifth generation computers. [2 marks]
(c) State ONE contribution each of Charles Babbage and Blaise Pascal to the development of computers. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) First generation: vacuum tubes
1 mark: (a) Second generation: transistors
1 mark: (a) Third generation: integrated circuits
1 mark: (a) Fourth generation: microprocessors (very large scale integration)
1 mark: (b) Artificial intelligence (ability to reason, recognise speech or learn)
1 mark: (b) Very fast, small and powerful; use of parallel processing or natural language
2 marks: (c) Babbage designed the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine, with a store (memory) and mill (processor), so he is called the father of the computer
2 marks: (c) Pascal built the Pascaline, a mechanical machine that could add and subtract
questions.explanation: Each generation is marked by a new technology. Babbage and Pascal designed early calculating machines that led to modern computers.

questions.stem:
(a) Define data and information. [4 marks]
(b) List in order the stages of the data processing cycle. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Data are raw, unprocessed facts and figures
2 marks: (a) Information is processed data that is meaningful and useful
1 mark: (b) Data gathering
1 mark: (b) Data collation
1 mark: (b) Input
1 mark: (b) Processing
1 mark: (b) Storage
1 mark: (b) Output
questions.explanation: Data becomes information after passing through the stages of the data processing cycle.

questions.stem:
(a) What is an operating system? [2 marks]
(b) Name four examples of operating systems. [4 marks]
(c) State four functions of an operating system. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) An operating system is system software that manages the computer's hardware and software and lets the user communicate with the computer
1 mark: (b) Windows
1 mark: (b) Linux
1 mark: (b) DOS
1 mark: (b) Unix, Android or macOS
1 mark: (c) Resource allocation (sharing processor time and memory)
1 mark: (c) File management
1 mark: (c) Monitoring devices and detecting errors
1 mark: (c) Providing a user interface / running utilities / booting the computer
questions.explanation: The operating system is the most important system software; it controls the computer and provides a platform for application programs.

questions.stem:
(a) Arrange the following units from smallest to largest: gigabyte, bit, kilobyte, nibble, megabyte, byte. [3 marks]
(b) Convert: (i) 3 bytes to bits (ii) 5 KB to bytes (iii) 6144 MB to GB. [6 marks]
(c) What is a byte? [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Bit, nibble, byte, kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte
2 marks: (b)(i) 3 x 8 = 24 bits
2 marks: (b)(ii) 5 x 1024 = 5120 bytes
2 marks: (b)(iii) 6144 / 1024 = 6 GB
1 mark: (c) A byte is a group of 8 bits (enough to store one character)
questions.explanation: Each storage unit is 1024 times the one before it, except that a nibble is 4 bits and a byte is 8 bits.

questions.stem:
(a) Write a BASIC program that accepts the length and breadth of a rectangle and prints its area. [6 marks]
(b) State the function of each of these statements: (i) REM (ii) INPUT (iii) PRINT. [3 marks]
(c) Write the BASIC expression for: (a + b) squared. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) 10 REM PROGRAM TO FIND AREA OF A RECTANGLE (or any suitable remark)
1 mark: (a) 20 INPUT L
1 mark: (a) 30 INPUT B (or INPUT L, B on one line)
1 mark: (a) 40 LET A = L * B
1 mark: (a) 50 PRINT A (or PRINT "AREA ="; A)
1 mark: (a) 60 END
1 mark: (b)(i) REM writes remarks/comments that are not executed
1 mark: (b)(ii) INPUT allows the user to enter data while the program runs
1 mark: (b)(iii) PRINT displays output on the screen
3 marks: (c) (A + B) ^ 2 (accept (A + B) * (A + B))
questions.explanation: A simple BASIC program reads data with INPUT, calculates with LET and shows results with PRINT, ending with END.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a computer virus? [2 marks]
(b) State four sources of computer viruses. [4 marks]
(c) State two warning signs of a virus and name two anti-virus programs. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A computer virus is a harmful program that copies itself and spreads, damaging files or the operation of the computer
1 mark: (b) Infected flash drives, CDs or diskettes
1 mark: (b) E-mail attachments
1 mark: (b) Internet downloads
1 mark: (b) Illegal (pirated) copies of software
1 mark: (c) Warning sign, e.g. slow response time or strange characters on the screen
1 mark: (c) Another sign, e.g. files not saving completely, missing files or corrupted set-up
1 mark: (c) Anti-virus 1, e.g. Norton AntiVirus
1 mark: (c) Anti-virus 2, e.g. McAfee VirusScan, Kaspersky, Avast, Dr Solomon's Toolkit
questions.explanation: Viruses spread through infected media, e-mails and downloads, and anti-virus programs detect and remove them.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four computer professionals and state the job of each. [8 marks]
(b) Name two computer professional bodies in Nigeria. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Programmer
1 mark: (a) Writes computer programs
1 mark: (a) System analyst
1 mark: (a) Studies an organisation's system and designs computer solutions
1 mark: (a) Computer engineer or technician
1 mark: (a) Builds, repairs and maintains hardware
1 mark: (a) Computer operator, educator or manager
1 mark: (a) Correct job description
1 mark: (b) Nigeria Computer Society (NCS)
1 mark: (b) Computer Professionals Registration Council of Nigeria (CPN), IMIS or Nigeria Internet Group (NIG)
questions.explanation: There are many career opportunities in computing, and professional bodies guide and regulate the profession.

questions.stem:
(a) Define the internet and the World Wide Web. [4 marks]
(b) List the main steps in creating an e-mail account. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The internet is the largest computer network in the world, linking millions of computers
2 marks: (a) The World Wide Web is the collection of linked web pages and websites accessed through the internet with a browser
1 mark: (b) Connect to the internet and open a web browser
1 mark: (b) Go to the website of an e-mail provider (e.g. Gmail or Yahoo)
1 mark: (b) Click Create account / Sign up
1 mark: (b) Fill in personal details such as name and date of birth
1 mark: (b) Choose a user name and a strong password
1 mark: (b) Complete verification, accept the terms and click to finish
questions.explanation: An e-mail account is created on a provider's website by filling a sign-up form and choosing a user name and password.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). Mr Eze records his provision shop's sales in Excel. Column A has item names (A2:A6), column B the quantity sold (B2:B6) and column C the unit price in naira (C2:C6).
(a) Write the formula in D2 to calculate the amount for the first item. [2 marks]
(b) Explain how to copy the formula in D2 to D3:D6. [2 marks]
(c) Write formulas to find (i) the total amount in D7 (ii) the highest amount in D8 (iii) the number of items in D9. [6 marks]
(d) How would you save the workbook with the name SHOP SALES? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) =B2*C2
2 marks: (b) Select D2 and drag the fill handle down to D6 (or copy D2 and paste into D3:D6)
2 marks: (c)(i) =SUM(D2:D6)
2 marks: (c)(ii) =MAX(D2:D6)
2 marks: (c)(iii) =COUNT(D2:D6) (accept =COUNTA(A2:A6))
2 marks: (d) Click File, Save As (or Ctrl + S), type SHOP SALES as the file name and click Save
questions.explanation: Formulas start with =, use cell references, and can be copied with the fill handle; SUM, MAX and COUNT summarise the data.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). The number of students in JSS 1, JSS 2 and JSS 3 of a school are typed in Excel in cells A1:B4, with headings in row 1.
(a) Describe how to create a column chart from the data. [4 marks]
(b) Describe how to add the chart title 'Students per Class' and axis titles. [4 marks]
(c) State one reason for adding a legend to a chart. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Select the data range A1:B4
1 mark: (a) Click the Insert tab
1 mark: (a) Choose Column (bar) chart
1 mark: (a) Select the type of column chart required
1 mark: (b) Click on the chart to select it
1 mark: (b) Use Chart Elements / Layout to add a Chart Title
1 mark: (b) Type 'Students per Class'
1 mark: (b) Add axis titles in the same way, e.g. Class and Number of students
2 marks: (c) A legend explains what each colour or pattern in the chart represents
questions.explanation: Charts are created from selected data through the Insert tab and made clear with titles, axis labels and legends.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). Aisha wants to type a letter to her principal in Microsoft Word.
(a) Describe how she can start Microsoft Word and open a new blank document. [2 marks]
(b) Describe how she can (i) centre the heading (ii) make the heading bold (iii) change the font size to 14. [6 marks]
(c) How can she print two copies of the letter? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Click Start (or double-click the Word icon), select Microsoft Word and choose Blank document
2 marks: (b)(i) Select the heading and click Center (or press Ctrl + E)
2 marks: (b)(ii) Select the heading and click Bold (or press Ctrl + B)
2 marks: (b)(iii) Select the text and choose 14 from the Font Size box
2 marks: (c) Click File, Print (or Ctrl + P), set Copies to 2 and click Print
questions.explanation: Word processors format text with commands on the Home tab and print through the Print dialog.

questions.stem:
Computer studies (answer in writing). Emeka wants to draw the Nigerian flag in Microsoft Paint.
(a) Name four Paint tools he will need and state what each is used for. [8 marks]
(b) How will he save the picture with the name MY FLAG? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Rectangle tool
1 mark: (a) To draw the outline of the flag and its three vertical sections
1 mark: (a) Line tool
1 mark: (a) To draw straight dividing lines
1 mark: (a) Fill with colour (paint bucket)
1 mark: (a) To fill the outer sections green and the middle white
1 mark: (a) Colour palette, eraser or select tool
1 mark: (a) To choose colours / correct mistakes / move the drawing
2 marks: (b) Click File, Save As, type MY FLAG, choose a picture format and click Save
questions.explanation: Simple shapes are drawn with the shape and line tools and coloured with the fill tool, then saved with a file name.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following database terms with an example from a school database: (i) field (ii) record (iii) key field. [6 marks]
(b) Name two forms of database. [2 marks]
(c) Name one database package. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) Field: one item of data about a person or thing
1 mark: (a)(i) e.g. Surname or Class
1 mark: (a)(ii) Record: all the fields about one person or thing
1 mark: (a)(ii) e.g. all the details of one student
1 mark: (a)(iii) Key field: a field that uniquely identifies each record
1 mark: (a)(iii) e.g. admission number
1 mark: (b) Flat file
1 mark: (b) Relational or hierarchical
2 marks: (c) Microsoft Access (accept dBase, MySQL, Oracle)
questions.explanation: Databases are organised into fields and records, with a unique key field for each record.
